nota: Words of this language that look borrowed from another language but do not exist there with that meaning, grouped by the language they imitate.

parole.testo: Borrowed from French autocar, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English autocar. By surface analysis, auto- + car.
Borrowed from French auto-stop, and this a pseudo-anglicism, from auto- (relating to cars) + English stop.
Borrowed from French basket, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English basketball.
Borrowed from French body and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English bodysuit.
Borrowed from French boxe, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English boxing.
Borrowed from English camping. The sense "campsite" is a pseudo-anglicism.
Borrowed from French cross, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English cross country. -cross exists in English to refer to cross country, but only as a suffix.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from dress. Doublet of direct.
Borrowed from French flipper, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English flipper.

parole.significato: scorer, player who scores many times.
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from goal + getter.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English holding company.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from jolly, derived from a clipping of English jolly joker, an older name for the joker card in a deck of cards.
Pseudo-anglicism; borrowed from French living or, less plausibly, an independent truncated borrowing from English living room.
Borrowed from French parking, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English parking.
Borrowed from French recordman, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from record + -man.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from set + ball. Compare Slovak setbal.
Borrowed from French slip, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English slip.
Borrowed from French talkie-walkie, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an inversion of English walkie-talkie.
Borrowed from French top-modèle, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English top + English model.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from training.
Borrowed from French vidéoclip, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English videoclip.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from volleyball.

nota_romeno: Romanian is left out of every ranking as a receiving language: its Wiktionary editors credit French with 28,409 borrowed words (they give an origin for 94% of its entries), including international learned words, and that would crowd out everything else.
